_comment: Clarity in the Quran playlist structure, 2026-08-17. The channel had ZERO playlists against 13 long-form videos. Created by automation/clarity_playlists.py.
_why_playlists: This is a long-form channel by the owner's explicit direction (2026-08-17: 'No need shorts, I need this to remain a long form channel'), and playlists are the single largest structural lever long-form has that Shorts does not. Three effects: autoplay carries a viewer from one video into the next, so session time compounds instead of ending at one video; a playlist is its own indexed entity that ranks in search separately from the videos in it; and grouping related uploads gives YouTube a topic-cluster signal a flat upload feed never provides.
_ordering: Each list opens with its strongest performer. A playlist's first video is what carries the rest — YouTube surfaces the playlist through it, and a viewer who arrives on a proven video is the one most likely to continue. Order after that is descending views, so the drop-off is gradual rather than a cliff.
_naming: Titles are written for search intent rather than for internal tidiness, because the playlist title is itself indexed. 'What the Quran Says About Your Emotions' is a phrase people type; 'Emotions Series' is not.

playlists.title: What the Quran Says About Your Emotions
playlists.description:
Anger, anxiety, depression, and the feeling that Allah has turned away — what the Quran actually says about each, verse by verse, in plain language.

No jargon. No rulings. Just the text and what it means.
playlists._why: The channel's strongest cluster by a wide margin: 1,027 of 2,473 lifetime views sit in these four. Anger alone carries 846 and leads the list, so the playlist has a real entry point rather than a cold start.

playlists.title: Stories of the Prophets in the Quran
playlists.description:
The prophets, the nations before us, and the patterns the Quran repeats on purpose — explained verse by verse.

Every episode traces the story back to the Arabic and the ayat it comes from.
playlists._why: Two 190-view videos plus the newest upload, which covers Sulayman and the jinn and belongs here on subject. Gives the 16 August video — the best-packaged on the channel — a route to viewers who arrive on the older two.

playlists.title: Money and Provision in the Quran
playlists.description:
Wealth, rizq, riba and barakah — what the Quran says about money, and the Arabic that changes how the verses read.

For anyone who has wondered whether it is allowed to want more.
playlists._why: 225-view opener. A tight, high-intent pair: people searching Islamic money questions are a distinct audience from people searching emotional ones, and mixing them would weaken both lists.

playlists.title: Questions Muslims Actually Ask
playlists.description:
The questions people search for privately and rarely ask out loud — answered from the Quran, without judgement and without a ruling.

What the text says, and what it does not.
playlists._why: The remaining four, which share an intent rather than a topic: each is a private question someone types into a search bar. Naming that honestly is what makes the list findable.

_coverage: All 13 long-form uploads appear in exactly one playlist. The three Shorts are deliberately excluded — the owner has set a long-form direction, and mixing Shorts into these lists would break the autoplay run that is the whole point.
_privacy: Playlists are created PUBLIC. A private playlist is invisible to search and to autoplay, which would defeat every reason for making them.
_link_titles: Short display names used in the WATCH NEXT block. Full titles are too long to read as a link list — several run past 60 characters — and a wall of long titles is skimmed past. These are lowercase-leaning and descriptive so the block reads as a menu, not a second title card.

_crosslink_marker: Sentinel that makes the block replaceable. Everything from this line to the end of the description is the generated block, so a re-run rewrites it instead of appending a second copy. Chosen to be visually distinct and unlikely to occur in hand-written copy.
_crosslink_placement: APPENDED at the end, never inserted near the top. The first two or three lines of a description are what YouTube shows as the search snippet, and these descriptions open with genuinely good hooks — 'Somebody watching this has paid money to have a jinn removed.' Pushing that down to gain a slightly higher link position would trade the thing that earns the click for the thing that earns the second view.
_description_cap: YouTube caps descriptions at 5,000 characters and rejects the whole update past it. StCW3ERkWwc already sits at 4,649, so the block cannot be assumed to fit. clarity_crosslinks.py budgets 4,900 and drops individual links until the block fits, reporting what it dropped.
